## Setup

```{r setup}
library(performance)
library(lme4)
library(draft)
```

## Models

```{r models}
# Simple linear model
m_lm <- lm(mpg ~ wt + cyl + am, data = mtcars)

# Nested models for comparison
m_lm_null <- lm(mpg ~ 1, data = mtcars)
m_lm_wt   <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)
m_lm_full <- lm(mpg ~ wt + cyl + am, data = mtcars)

# Mixed model — r2() returns marginal + conditional (Nakagawa), also has ICC
m_lmer <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject), data = sleepstudy)

# Logistic model — r2() returns Tjur's R2
m_glm <- glm(am ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars, family = binomial)
```

## model_performance()

Full suite of fit indices for a single model. Includes R2, ICC (for mixed models),
AIC, BIC, RMSE, Sigma, and more — varies by model type.

```{r model-performance}
perf_lm   <- model_performance(m_lm)
perf_lmer <- model_performance(m_lmer)
perf_glm  <- model_performance(m_glm)

perf_lm
perf_lmer
perf_glm

# Class and available fields — drives how the inspector renders chips
class(perf_lm)
names(perf_lm)

class(perf_lmer)
names(perf_lmer)   # should include R2_marginal, R2_conditional, ICC

class(perf_glm)
names(perf_glm)    # should include Tjur_R2, Log_loss, AUC
```

## compare_performance()

Comparison table across nested or non-nested models, ranked by fit.

```{r compare-performance}
comparison <- compare_performance(m_lm_null, m_lm_wt, m_lm_full, rank = TRUE)
comparison

class(comparison)
names(comparison)
str(comparison)
```

## What does draft see?

```{r for-draft}
# Flatten to list — this is what the inspector will work from
as.list(perf_lm)
as.list(perf_lmer)
as.data.frame(comparison)
```

## draft::launch_app() — manual test

Uncomment to launch the app and inspect these objects.

```{r launch, eval=FALSE}
draft::launch_app()
```
